sections.body:
This is a story about Leo the lion and Mimi the mouse. Leo is the biggest animal in the meadow. Mimi is one of the smallest.

A good story has a shape. It has a beginning, a middle, and an end. The beginning tells you who the characters are. The middle brings a problem. The end fixes the problem in a way you did not expect.

This story has that shape. In the beginning, Leo catches Mimi. In the middle, Mimi helps Leo escape. In the end, Leo learns that small friends matter too.

The animals talk in short sentences here. The sentences are easy to say out loud. Try reading them with a big voice for Leo and a small voice for Mimi.

Listen first. Then tell the story back to someone. That is how a story becomes yours.
examples: This story has a beginning, a middle and an end.
Leo is the lion, and Mimi is the mouse.
I can tell this story again tomorrow.
sections.heading: What this story is about

sections.body:
Leo the lion sleeps in the warm grass. His mane is like a golden ring. His roar can be heard from the far hill.

One hot afternoon, Mimi the mouse runs across Leo's nose.

Mimi does not see Leo. Mimi is looking for a crumb of bread near the foot of the oak tree. Leo opens one big eye.

Then a paw comes down, and Mimi is under it.

Mimi squeaks. Leo is sorry. He lifts his paw and lets Mimi go. Leo laughs at himself. What is a lion to fear a mouse?

But Mimi is not angry. Mimi says: one day I will help you, and then you will be glad.

Leo laughs again. A mouse helping a lion. That is a funny idea.

But Leo keeps Mimi's words in his head.
examples: Mimi ran right across Leo's nose.
Leo is sorry, so he lifts his paw.
One day I will help you.
sections.heading: The beginning: a paw on a tail

sections.body:
Some days later, Leo wakes up in the middle of the night. Something has caught him.

It is a net. A hunter has thrown a net over Leo, and Leo cannot get out. Leo pulls. Leo roars. The net is strong.

Leo thinks about the day he caught Mimi. He calls out into the dark. But the forest is asleep.

Then he hears a small sound. It is not a bird. It is a mouse.

Mimi hears Leo too. Mimi comes running. Mimi finds the knot of the net. Mimi bites the rope. Mimi bites and bites with all her tiny teeth.

The rope breaks.

Leo walks out of the net, free. He looks down at his small friend. Leo says nothing for a long moment.
examples: A net has caught Leo, and he cannot get out.
Leo called out into the dark.
Mimi bit the rope with all her tiny teeth.
sections.heading: The middle: a strange sound in the night

sections.body:
Then Leo says the words Mimi wanted to hear: you were right, and I am glad you helped me.

Leo was wrong that day. A mouse was not too small. A mouse was exactly the right size.

After that, Leo and Mimi are friends. Leo walks slowly so Mimi can keep up. Mimi rides on Leo's mane. When the rain comes, Leo lies down so Mimi can sleep under his warm chin.

The meadow tells the story to everyone now. The birds sing it. The fox tells it to his cubs. And when a little animal feels too small to matter, the meadow tells them about Mimi.

Being small is not the same as being powerless.
examples: You were right, and I am glad you helped me.
Leo walked slowly so Mimi could keep up.
Being small is not the same as being powerless.
sections.heading: The surprise: the small one saves the big one

sections.body:
These are the words you will meet in this story. Learn them here, and you can use them in your own sentences.

A **net** is a rope net. It is strong and light. People use nets to catch animals, and fishermen use nets to catch fish.

To **gnaw** is to bite something again and again until it breaks. Mice gnaw cheese. In this story, Mimi gnaws a rope.

A **roar** is the deep loud sound a lion makes. It can travel a long way across the meadow.

A **favour** is a kind thing you do for someone. You do not have to be paid back right away.

A **purr** is the small happy sound a cat makes when it is comfortable. Many animals make a sound like this when they are glad.
examples: A net is a strong rope net.
The mouse gnawed the rope until it broke.
The lion's roar was heard from the far hill.
sections.heading: The words inside this story

terms.example: The hunter threw a net over Leo.
terms.gloss: A rope net. It is strong and light, and it can hold a big animal.

terms.example: Mimi gnawed the rope until it broke.
terms.gloss: To bite something again and again until it breaks.

terms.example: Leo's roar woke the whole meadow.
terms.gloss: The deep loud sound a lion makes. It travels a long way.

terms.example: Mimi did Leo a favour that night.
terms.gloss: A kind thing you do for someone. You can do it without being paid back at once.

terms.example: Mimi purred when Leo lay down to sleep.
terms.gloss: The small happy sound an animal makes when it feels comfortable.

sections.body:
What did Leo learn? Leo learned that size is not the same as worth. A tiny mouse with tiny teeth can do what a huge lion cannot.

And Mimi learned something too. A good friend helps even when the help looks too small to matter.

Here is how to tell this story to someone. Keep the order, and the surprise will land in the right place.

Start with who the story is about. Tell the problem in the middle. Save the surprise for last. Then say the small lesson in one short sentence.

The lesson of this story is this: small does not mean powerless.
examples: The story starts with a lion and a mouse.
The mouse saves the lion in the end.
sections.heading: The small lesson, and how to tell the story
steps: Start by naming the characters: Leo the lion and Mimi the mouse.
Tell the beginning: Leo catches Mimi and lets her go.
Tell the middle: Leo is caught in a net in the night.
End with the surprise and the lesson: small does not mean powerless.

item.summary: A lion catches a small mouse, and the mouse promises to help him one day. Follow the lion and the mouse from the sunny grass to the hunter's net, where the smallest friend does the biggest job. After reading, you can retell the story, use its new words, and tell its lesson.
item.title: The Lion and the Clever Mouse
